summary: D.C.'s delegate race is drawing attention as the election approaches, with coverage of candidate Robert White's efforts regarding his eligibility and broader discussions of voting and the delegate position itself. Recent headlines also reflect on the legacy of longtime Delegate Eleanor Holmes Norton. Without statehood, D.C. residents have no senators, and their one delegate to the House cannot vote on the House floor.
